summary.en: Inspect named columns, select by labels or positions and add a derived measurement safely.
summary.bn: নামসহ কলাম দেখো, label বা অবস্থান দিয়ে বাছো আর নতুন মাপের কলাম যোগ করো।

notes: Python syntax works on 3.10+; Python 3.12 is recommended.
Use NumPy 2.0+, pandas 2.2+, scikit-learn 1.5+ and Matplotlib 3.8+ on a compatible Python.

sections.title: Predict both the values and the labels
Use each selector for its own question

examples.title: A labelled table and its first rows
examples.explanationHtml: A DataFrame is a table; selecting one named column returns a Series. The row labels here are 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50, so they differ from zero-based positions.

examples.title: Inspect types, counts and numeric spread
examples.explanationHtml: info writes column types and present-value counts to info.txt. describe computes numeric summaries. Five sizes sum to 22, giving mean 4.4; this says nothing about an unseen fruit.

examples.title: Select using labels and positions
examples.explanationHtml: loc selects labels and includes the endpoint in this ordered label slice. iloc selects positions and excludes the stop. Double brackets preserve a two-dimensional table.

examples.title: Filter and add a unit conversion
examples.explanationHtml: Only the last two fruits meet both conditions. Parentheses keep the comparisons together. Copying before adding size_mm makes the separate result explicit.

practice.title: Select by row label
practice.statementHtml: Use the table of sizes [2,3,4,6,7] and sweetness [3,2,3,7,8] with labels [10,20,30,40,50]. Read one valid row label and print its size and sweetness separated by one space.
hints: Use loc for a label; iloc would interpret the number as a position.

practice.title: Convert selected fruit sizes
practice.statementHtml: Read an integer size cutoff. Load tiny_fruits.csv, retain sizes at least the cutoff, and add size_mm = size_cm * 10. Print label:size_mm on one line per retained fruit, preserving file order; print none if no row qualifies.
hints: Create a copy with loc before assigning the conversion column.

practice.title: Explain two row slices
practice.statementHtml: For ordered row labels [10,20,30,40,50], compare loc[20:40] with iloc[1:3].
hints: The stop label and stop position obey different rules.
practice.answerHtml: loc[20:40] includes labels 20, 30 and 40. iloc[1:3] includes positions 1 and 2, whose labels are 20 and 30. The stop position 3 is excluded. After changing labels, a positional selection and a label selection need not select the same records.

practice.title: Two simultaneous filters
practice.statementHtml: Write a condition retaining fruits with size at least 4 and sweetness at least 7. Explain why Python and fails here.
hints: pandas combines Boolean Series element by element with &.
practice.answerHtml: Use (frame["size_cm"] >= 4) & (frame["sweetness"] >= 7). Each comparison returns a Boolean Series. and asks for one truth value for a whole Series, which is ambiguous. Parentheses ensure each comparison is evaluated before the bitwise combination.

quiz.prompt: What does selecting frame["size_cm"] usually return?
options: A scalar for every possible frame
quiz.explanation: One named column becomes a Series carrying its row index. Double brackets can keep a one-column DataFrame.

quiz.prompt: Why can frame.head() miss a serious data problem?
options: It previews only the first rows
It only reads the final row
quiz.explanation: An outlier near the end will not appear in the first five rows. Previewing is a starting point, not full validation.

quiz.prompt: Which inspection reports non-null counts and column types?
quiz.explanation: info summarises the structure and present-cell counts. It does not know whether 30 study hours per day is plausible.

quiz.prompt: What is the stop rule for an iloc positional slice?
options: The stop position is always included
quiz.explanation: iloc follows Python’s half-open positional slicing. loc label slices have different endpoint behaviour.

quiz.prompt: Which expression combines two rowwise pandas conditions?
quiz.explanation: The ampersand combines Boolean Series element by element. Parentheses prevent operator precedence from changing the comparisons.

quiz.prompt: What does a new size_mm column computed as size_cm * 10 mean?
options: A fruit grows ten times larger
The same size expressed in millimetres
quiz.explanation: This is a unit conversion, so record the new unit in the name or description. It is not a new independent observation.

quiz.prompt: Why select [["size_cm"]] with double brackets when a table is required?
options: The result keeps both row and column dimensions
It converts all cells to strings
quiz.explanation: A list of column names selects a DataFrame, including when the list contains only one name.

quiz.prompt: Which size is selected by the row label 20?
quiz.explanation: loc finds label 20, whose size is 6. It does not treat 20 as a row position.
quiz.code:
import pandas as pd
f = pd.DataFrame({"size": [2, 6, 7]}, index=[10, 20, 30])
print(f.loc[20, "size"])

quiz.prompt: Which row labels survive this positional slice?
quiz.explanation: Positions zero and one correspond to labels 10 and 20. Position two is excluded.
quiz.code:
import pandas as pd
f = pd.DataFrame({"size": [2, 6, 7]}, index=[10, 20, 30])
print(f.iloc[0:2].index.tolist())

quiz.prompt: How many rows remain after the sweetness filter?
quiz.explanation: Sweetness values 7 and 8 meet the threshold, so two rows remain.
quiz.code:
import pandas as pd
f = pd.DataFrame({"sweet": [3, 2, 3, 7, 8]})
print(len(f.loc[f["sweet"] >= 7]))

keyPoints.en: A DataFrame is a table and a Series is a labelled sequence.
keyPoints.bn: DataFrame একটি টেবিল, Series label-সহ একটি ধারাবাহিক মানের তালিকা।

keyPoints.en: Row labels need not equal row positions.
keyPoints.bn: সারির label আর অবস্থান এক হওয়া জরুরি নয়।

keyPoints.en: Use loc for labels and iloc for positions.
keyPoints.bn: label দিয়ে বাছতে loc, অবস্থান দিয়ে বাছতে iloc ব্যবহার করো।

keyPoints.en: Inspect structure and summaries before interpreting measurements.
keyPoints.bn: মাপের অর্থ বোঝার আগে টেবিলের গঠন আর সারাংশ দেখো।

keyPoints.en: Parenthesise comparisons before combining Boolean Series.
keyPoints.bn: Boolean Series মেলানোর আগে প্রতিটি তুলনা বন্ধনীতে রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Choose an explicit destination for a derived column.
keyPoints.bn: নতুন হিসাবের কলাম কোন টেবিলে যাবে, স্পষ্ট করো।

examQuestions.question: Sizes are [2,3,4,6,7] and sweetness values are [3,2,3,7,8]. Apply size>=4 and sweetness>=7, then convert the selected sizes to millimetres.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Rows with sizes 4, 6 and 7 pass the size test. Only sizes 6 and 7 also pass the sweetness test. The selected pairs are (6,7) and (7,8). Multiply centimetres by ten to get sizes [60,70] mm. Their original labels or indices must travel with the selected rows.

examQuestions.question: Explain what head, info and describe can each tell you, and one limit of each.
examQuestions.answerHtml: head previews the first rows but may miss rare cases. info reports column types and non-null counts but does not verify measurement meaning. describe summarises numeric spread by default but does not show every row or establish causes. Use the three together before deciding which further checks are needed.

examQuestions.question: Why make an explicit copy of a filtered DataFrame before adding a derived column?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The copy communicates that the selected table is independent and intended for separate editing. Assigning with chosen["size_mm"] = chosen["size_cm"] * 10 then has a clear destination. If the goal is to edit the original table, use one frame.loc[mask, "size_mm"] assignment instead of chained indexing. pandas copy behaviour varies by version and Copy-on-Write mode.
